1. The main object is a stack of banknotes on a blue base. It stands for Nina's money, an investment or savings pot that starts at $92,000. The small figure is Nina, and the building next to it is probably a home or workplace. The label says "Nina · ILLUSTRATIVE", so the numbers are an example and not real data.

2. The stack's height and colour change from frame to frame. The dates run from Nov 2007 to Nov 2017.
   - In Nov 2007 the stack is green and sits right at the line.
   - In Oct 2008 it is shorter and turns orange/gold. This looks like a loss, probably the 2008 crash.
   - In Dec 2009 it is still orange and about as low. A single bill floats above it.
   - In Aug 2011 it is green again and a bit taller than the start.
   - In May 2014 it is much taller.
   - In Nov 2017 it is far taller and runs off the top of the frame.

   So the money dropped during the crash and then recovered and grew a lot. Orange means below the starting value, and green means above it. The loose bills that drift in and out look like contributions or gains.

3. The horizontal translucent line is a reference level at the starting balance. The label "$92,000 start" marks it. Below the line means Nina is down from her starting amount, and above it means she is up. The 2008–2009 stack falls under the line, and the later stacks rise well above it.

4. A few things are confusing.
   - The frames show no dollar amount for the current stack, so the size of the loss and the gain can't be read. The only number is "$92,000 start".
   - The orange colour has no legend. I'm assuming it means "below start".
   - The line seems to sit at a different height in the top and bottom rows. This is probably camera framing.
   - In the last frame the stack goes off the top of the image, so its peak is cut off.
   - The building and figure have no label, so what they mean is unclear.
   - The floating bills have no explanation.
